entries.root_cause: The composed Monitoring-to-Alerting publication conformance executed the accepted Wave 2 outbox migration and all Wave 4 Monitoring migrations, but its workflow path filters watched only bridge-local files. A substrate change could therefore invalidate the composed runtime while the bridge-specific gate was never scheduled.

The bridge upgraded same-signature functions to SECURITY DEFINER with CREATE OR REPLACE and revoked only PUBLIC afterward. PostgreSQL preserves explicit function ACLs across CREATE OR REPLACE, so a pre-existing named EXECUTE grantee could retain direct invocation authority over the newly privileged publication helper and forge tenant-scoped integration events.
horizontal_audit: all CREATE OR REPLACE SECURITY DEFINER migrations
pre-existing function ACLs and named EXECUTE grants

entries.root_cause: The ACL preflight allowed the canonical recovery authority as a retained named EXECUTE grantee but did not reject EXECUTE WITH GRANT OPTION. CREATE OR REPLACE would preserve that grantability, allowing the recovery authority to delegate a cross-tenant SECURITY DEFINER recovery entry point to arbitrary roles after commit.

The publication-specific falsifiers were credited in the learning ledger but were only executed by the D4-C workflow, whose path filters did not observe publication SQL, workflow, or ACL-conformance inputs. Publication-only regressions could therefore weaken permanent guardrails without executing the credited falsifier in the affected PR.

Pre-elevation ACL validation covered only functions that already existed. On a first-time CREATE FUNCTION, the installer role's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES could inject a named EXECUTE grant before ownership transfer; revoking only PUBLIC afterward would preserve that unexpected authority through COMMIT on the new SECURITY DEFINER function.

The dedicated publication executor was validated only by role attributes and memberships before receiving outbox privileges. If that role already owned another callable SECURITY DEFINER routine, the new table grants could empower the unrelated routine to forge publication state even though every bridge function itself passed ACL checks.

The dedicated-owner closure inspected only pg_proc. A pre-existing view or other owner-mediated object owned by the executor could therefore remain shared to another role and begin exercising newly granted outbox authority through owner privilege as soon as the migration granted storage access.
horizontal_audit: schemas types sequences and other owner-mediated objects
